newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Cargill sees Asian demand rising for feed/meal.
newsitem.headline: Cargill sees Asian demand rising for feed/meal.

text.p: Asian demand for feed grains and protein meal to produce meat and poultry products will expand strongly because of population growth and rapid urbanisation, a senior economist with Cargill Asia Pacific Ltd said on Wednesday.

Michael Humphrey, a senior economist with Cargill, said in a report to an Asia Oilseeds conference in Singapore that growing demand, rising incomes and urbanisation "are driving the significant increases in demand" for food products throughout Asia.
"Estimates for gross domestic product (GDP) growth range from 4-5 percent per annum for the Asia-Pacific region over the next five years," Humphrey said in his report.
In the case of China, while corn output has increased 21 percent since 1990, domestic consumption has risen by an estimated 45 percent, he said.

"While a more favourable corn crop may be the case in 1996, the demand for corn to meet the rapidly expanding needs of the feed industry will likely quickly take off those corn supplies," Humphrey said in the report.

Indonesia corn imports have risen to 1.5 million tonnes in 1996 from 135,000 tonnes in 1990. Expansion of the feed industry in Malaysia has resulted in corn imports rising to about 2.6 million tonnes this year from 1.5 million tonnes in 1990.
Thailand, which used to be a major corn exporter, is beginning to feel the pinch to meet the requirements of its poultry and swine industries.
In oilmeal production, Asian production exceeded consumption until 1995.

"In 1996, consumption exceeded production," Humphrey said. "Meal imports have more than doubled from 1.7 million tonnes in 1990 to 2.7 million tonnes by 1996. Due to the expanding feed industry, meal import demand will continue to increase."
One striking example is Indonesia, where meal imports have tripled since 1990 to 900,000 tonnes this year.
"Expansion of the feed industry in Asia, particularly in Southeast Asia, is critical to meet future requirements for vegetable protein," Humphrey said.
Production of poultry, swine and aquaculture will be the sectors undergoing expansion in Asia, he added.
